schema.name: appliccrossreftable
schema.title: Applicability Cross-reference Table
schema.definition: The Applicability Cross-reference Table (ACT) data module is used to declare product attributes.

schema.name: brex
schema.title: Business Rules Exchange
schema.definition: The mechanism is a means to communicate business rules that have been developed and agreed within a project or organization.

schema.name: checklist
schema.title: Maintenance Checklists and Inspections
schema.definition: This Schema is used to capture and represent maintenance planning information but includes key elements to provide additional functionality. It provides the ability to reduce failure by providing a list of operations or checks to be performed for maintaining the Product. The schema can be used for checklist and inspection information such as scheduled inspection and maintenance conditions necessary to keep the equipment in serviceable condition. It includes a special category to identify in what instances the equipment is not ready or usable.

schema.name: comment
schema.title: Comment
schema.definition: Commenting and reporting on issues raised on data modules or publication modules during the verification process and the in-service phase of the Product can be done using the comment form. This form is compiled by the commenting authority and sent to the issuing authority of the data modules or publication modules. The comment form is also used to provide a response to the originator of the comment.

schema.name: condcrossreftable
schema.title: Conditions Cross-reference Table
schema.definition: The Conditions Cross-reference Table (CCT) data module is used to declare conditions that have an affect on the applicability of data and is used to define the incorporation status for technical conditions.

schema.name: container
schema.title: Container
schema.definition: The container data module is a production management mechanism to associate several data modules representing the same data.

schema.name: crew
schema.title: Crew/Operator Information
schema.definition: The Crew Schema is provided for the production of Crew/Operator information such as description and operation of the Product, flight and sequential information.

schema.name: dc
schema.title: Dublin core
schema.definition: Dublin core metadata is specifically intended to support resource discovery. The elements represent a broad, interdisciplinary consensus about the core set of elements that are useful to support resource discovery.

schema.name: ddn
schema.title: Data Dispatch Note
schema.definition: The data dispatch note defines the sender, the receiver and the content of the dispatch.

schema.name: descript
schema.title: Descriptive
schema.definition: This Schema is used to capture and represent descriptive information.

schema.name: dml
schema.title: Data Management List
schema.definition:
A Data Management Requirement List (DMRL) is used to identify the required data modules and, by project decision, publication modules for a project. The data management requirement list supports planning, reporting, production and configuration control, especially in a work share environment. A data management requirement list can be generated in parts (eg, by partner companies for later merging) or in a complete form.
The purpose of a CSDB Status List (CSL) is to exchange information about the status of the CSDB.

schema.name: fault
schema.title: Fault Information
schema.definition: The fault Schema is used to capture and represent fault reporting, fault isolation and fault correlation information.

schema.name: ipd
schema.title: Illustrated Parts Data
schema.definition: The IPD Schema is to be used to capture and represent parts lists and IPD. This information can be drawn from an S2000M provisioning database or from engineering data for a non-S2000M project.

schema.name: learning
schema.title: Learning
schema.definition: In S1000D, the support for managing learning information reflects how the information is structured and managed in accordance with Sharable Content Object Reference Model (SCORM). The incentive is to use a CSDB for managing learning information with same degree of control as applied to the technical publications.

schema.name: pm
schema.title: Publication Module
schema.definition: In order to define, prepare and manage publications generated of data modules, S1000D uses the publication module.

schema.name: prdcrossreftable
schema.title: Products Cross-reference Table
schema.definition: The Products Cross-reference Table (PCT) data module is a repository of product instances and the values for product attributes and conditions for each product instance.

schema.name: proced
schema.title: Procedural
schema.definition: The procedural Schema is used to capture and represent procedural information. The granularity of maintenance procedural data modules must follow the breakdown reflected by the SNS and the information codes, and must reflect the tasks identified in the maintenance plan. The granularity of crew/operator procedural data modules must follow the breakdown reflected by the SNS and the information codes, and must reflect the operations identified.

schema.name: process
schema.title: Process
schema.definition: The S1000D process data module represents a procedural flow consisting of several data modules and/or steps that are sequenced. Decision points (branching), looping, and selective filtering are supported. An interface to external applications which can return results to direct procedural flow is supported. The process data module can be considered a procedural flow script.

schema.name: rdf
schema.title: Resource Description Framework
schema.definition: Resource Description Framework (RDF) is a framework for metadata providing interoperability between applications that exchange machine-understandable information on the web. RDF emphasizes facilities to enable automated processing of web resources and, as such, provides the basic building blocks for supporting the semantic web.##BREAK##In general, RDF provides the basis for generic tools for authoring, manipulating, and searching machine-understandable data on the web thereby promoting the transformation of the web into a machine-processable repository of information.

schema.name: schedul
schema.title: Maintenance Planning
schema.definition: This Schema is used to capture and represent maintenance planning information.

schema.name: scocontent
schema.title: SCORM content information
schema.definition: The SCO content Schema is composed of elements used to provide references to external SCO or S1000D managed references defining a hierarchy of training steps.

schema.name: scormcontentpackage
schema.title: SCORM Content Package Module
schema.definition: The SCPM is used to define the hierarchical structure of learning events within a course or learning product. To be more representative of how training is packaged for use in a Learning Management System (LMS), certain element names in the SCORM content package module have been modified, and new elements have been added.

schema.name: techrep
schema.title: Technical Information Repository
schema.definition: The technical information repository data module is used to capture and represent functional items and their properties.

schema.name: wrngdata
schema.title: Wiring Data
schema.definition: The wiring data Schema is used to capture and represent the wiring data of the Product such as wire data, harness data, electrical equipment data and standard parts data.

schema.name: wrngflds
schema.title: Wiring Data Description
schema.definition: The wiring data description Schema is used for configuration and declaration of the elements of the wiring data Schema.

schema.name: xcf
schema.title: WebCGM 2.0 XML Companion File
schema.definition: WebCGM 2.0 includes an external companion file that enables control of the behavior of the WebCGM viewer through an XML DOM interface.

schema.name: xlink
schema.title: XML Linking Language
schema.definition: Linkage within an IETP is specified using XLink attributes within the XML repository. Links must use the URN of the resource referenced, and can be created automatically from the content of the elements <dmRef>, <pmRef>, <externalPubRef>, <catalogSeqNumberRef>, <graphic>, <multimediaObject>, <symbol> and <internalRef>.
